clue.text: Louisa may be a successful author

definitions.text: Louisa may be a successful author

parts.words: Louisa may be a successful author
parts.note: surface reading: any woman called Louisa might go on to succeed as a writer
setter's reading: Louisa May is the first and middle name of the American novelist who wrote Little Women

explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case 'may' disguises a middle name: read it as May and the clue points to one famous nineteenth-century American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women, a hugely popular nineteenth-century novel, so she was indeed a successful writer.

clue.text: Care a bit about the cause of infection

indicators.note: 'about' can mean scattered around, so the preceding words are jumbled up

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone advising a little caution about whatever causes infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Microbes of this kind are a common source of disease, invading the body and making wounds or organs septic.

clue.text: Operated craft with a hundred that had married again

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to rewed is to marry once more

explanation.surface: A boat's company includes a hundred people who had each remarried.
explanation.definitionFit: To man a ship or boat is to staff it with a working team of sailors, so a vessel so staffed was operated.

indicators.note: to waste something is to ruin it, so the preceding letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A grubby bin for rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste receptacle' reads as one phrase meaning a bin, but 'waste' works on the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: This small dish is a container into which smokers tip cigarette ends and ash.

clue.text: Is back to cover distant journey

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it, so one piece goes outside the other
going back means the word is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone has returned to report on a long trip far away.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an expedition, typically in Africa, to watch or hunt wild animals, so it is a kind of long trip.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the chess piece that moves in straight lines
second meaning: a large fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: A crow's nest likened to a fortified stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook reads as the bird, but here it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece is commonly given this alternative name, and the same word is a medieval fortified stronghold of a lord.

clue.text: Big bird's a hit, of course!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a huge seabird of the southern oceans
second meaning: a golf score of three under par on a hole, achieved on a golf course

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a giant bird is obviously a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like 'naturally', but it means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the great wandering seabird, and in golf it is a score three strokes under par on one hole.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hackneyed, worn out from overuse

explanation.surface: Someone is exhausted, as they always are.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something trite and stale through overuse, and also something entirely ordinary and unremarkable.

parts.note: with means in the company of

explanation.surface: Someone goes forward with company without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means immediately, without any delay, a slightly formal word for at once.

definitions.note: the answer is a verb, 'is breathless'; the definition is an adjective

indicators.note: only a small portion of the following words is used, a stretch inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A competitor appears somewhat out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sits in particiPANT Seems; 'seems a bit' reads as 'appears somewhat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breathes in short, quick gasps after exertion is out of breath, which is what being breathless means.

indicators.note: something wandering moves about, so the letters drift out of order

explanation.surface: A ruler is described as having a roving celestial body.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was held by the Russian monarchs before 1917, an imperial ruler comparable to a Caesar.

indicators.note: 'sorted out' suggests rearranging, so those letters are put in a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Tidying things up and putting them back in the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept in a cupboard or warehouse for later use have been tucked away for safekeeping.

clue.text: Sailor relies sadly on one fast going down

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the preceding word is jumbled

explanation.surface: A seaman depends unhappily on someone who is quickly sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber descending a rock face on a rope is someone held fast to the line while dropping downward.

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: letters across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Things calm down readily in sheltered air.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is in settLE Easily.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side away from the wind is the side the wind blows towards, so it is downwind.

clue.text: Mean to turn up for musical performance

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: par is the average or normal level

explanation.surface: A nasty person shows up to a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as unkind, but it is the noun for an average.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of music with rhythmic spoken lyrics, so a piece of it is a kind of vocal performance.

clue.text: Preserve an icon cleric acquired initially in the Caribbean

definitions.note: describes a place found in that sea

parts.note: the indefinite article in short form

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A jar of jam and a holy image picked up by a priest on a Caribbean trip.
explanation.definitionFit: This large island nation lies in the western sea of the Antilles, south of Cuba, so it is a place there.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Little more than a plain gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: This French culinary term means a thin gravy made from meat juices, served as a light sauce.

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about their mum.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers being frenzied, uncontrolled or crazy, the same as being out of control.

clue.text: Medic rises to carry pupil, an oaf

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upward
carrying something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A doctor stands up to lift a student who is a lout.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner is the plate a British learner driver displays.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an insult for a dull, stupid or clumsy person, a lump of a fellow.

clue.text: Pure wit deployed to do the paperwork

indicators.note: deployed means moved into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Using sheer cleverness to get through the admin.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down in full written form, such as a report or notes, is to complete the written records.

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Reasons for holding back a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' reads as reasons, but it means tracts of land.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stretches of land considered for their physical features, which is what grounds can mean.

clue.text: Once more, good guy is opposed

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a crossword good guy

explanation.surface: A decent fellow objects yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition expresses opposition, as in voting the other way, so being so placed means being in opposition.

clue.text: One way to look at edge that's extended

parts.note: a side is an edge or border
long means stretched out at length

explanation.surface: A way of examining a border that has been lengthened.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance made out of the corner of the eye, often furtively, is a familiar manner of looking.

indicators.note: cultivated soil has been turned over, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener concludes that a fern has been grown deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence rather than being told it outright is to work something out logically.

indicators.note: maybe signals the letters could be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Assistance in getting slim, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something possible for someone is to assist them in doing it.

clue.text: Short bra undone and perhaps put by

indicators.note: a garment that is undone has come apart, so its letters are loosened
perhaps signals the letters could be in some other order

explanation.surface: Underwear left unfastened and maybe set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt or brusque manner is one that is rude through being too brief, and a sudden end is a quick one.

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A shining deity standing in for a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who composes books or articles is a creator of written works, which is exactly a writer.

indicators.note: sounding means what follows matters for how it is pronounced, not how it is spelt

explanation.surface: Someone glanced over, seeming irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance quickly or slyly, often through a gap, is a brief way of having looked.

clue.text: It's not on! Two thirds of all meats are for haggis

indicators.note: keeping two thirds of a three-letter word means one letter is dropped

parts.note: something not on is switched off

explanation.surface: An indignant protest that most meat goes into haggis.
explanation.walkthrough: Haggis is the Scottish dish of a sheep's heart, liver and lungs minced with oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ meats such as heart, liver and lungs make up haggis, and the collective word for such innards is this one.

clue.text: Avert rail disaster? Find alternative transport!

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge a train crash by choosing another way to get there.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying is a means of getting around that stands as an option instead of going by train.

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Keep singing until the monarch arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To warble with a rapid wavering of notes, as birds do, is a way of producing song.

indicators.note: something misused is handled wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone intimidated, badly treated and utterly amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe being overwhelmed with surprise or shock, utterly amazed.
